title: Gabber regular pairs cover the prime-to-ell alteration site
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Suppose that every affine coordinate ring of $S$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $Z$ be a nowhere dense closed subset of $S$, and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $S$. There are finitely many regular Noetherian schemes $T_b$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] and morphisms $q_b:T_b\to S$ which are objects of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ and form a covering for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. In particular every $q_b$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each $b$ there is a strict normal crossings boundary $H_b\subseteq T_b$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] whose support is $q_b^{-1}(Z)$.

source.place: Expose IX, Theorem 1.1, printed p. 131; the alteration category and topology are those of Expose II 1.2.2 and 2.3.1. Boundary is taken with reduced structure, as in VIII 4.1.4 and 4.2.2(i).

proof.text: Use [lem-per-uniformization-nodal-quotient-reduction]. Its hypothesis is an assertion about marked nodal quotient models, not uniformization for general schemes. We prove that hypothesis in Steps 2--6, with arbitrary data $Y,T,G,Y',b,C,f,D,\pi:C\to X$ and effective Cartier divisor $E$ exactly as introduced in its statement. In particular $Y$ is affine excellent regular, $Y'$ is the normalization in a connected finite etale $G$-torsor off $T$, $C$ is integral excellent, and $\pi^{-1}|E|\subseteq B:=|D|\cup f^{-1}b^{-1}|T|$. No regularity of $X=C/G$ is assumed.

The order of $G$ is a power of $\ell$, hence invertible on $Y$. Apply [lem-per-tame-normalization-log-regular] to $Y,T$ and the connected finite etale $G$-torsor $b^{-1}(Y\setminus|T|)\to Y\setminus|T|$. Its normalization is the given $Y'$, so $(Y',b^{-1}|T|)$ is a log regular pair. This step asserts log regularity of $Y'$, not regularity of its underlying scheme.

Apply [lem-trf-nodal-log-regularity] to $f:C\to Y'$ and the closed subset $b^{-1}|T|$, with the given marking $D$. The model supplies projectivity, hence properness, as well as flatness and finite presentation; all geometric fibres are nonempty connected nodal curves; $f$ is smooth away from $b^{-1}|T|$; and $D$ is effective Cartier, etale over $Y'$ and contained in the relative smooth locus. Thus $B$ is nowhere dense and $(C,B)$ is log regular. All conditions, including properness of the nodal morphism, are present in the model.

The action preserves $B$. It is free on $f^{-1}(b^{-1}(Y\setminus|T|))$: a geometric stabilizer there maps to the stabilizer of its image in the $G$-torsor, which is trivial. This open contains $C\setminus B$ and is dense by Step 3. Its order is invertible on $C$. The model assumes admissibility and the integral excellent scheme quotient $X$. The marked model includes separatedness and Noetherianity of $C$. Apply [lem-per-tame-log-quotient-modification] to obtain an integral excellent Noetherian $M$, a proper birational $\rho:M\to X$, and a log regular pair $(M,B_M)$ with $\rho^{-1}\pi(B)\subseteq B_M$. Since $\pi$ is surjective and $\pi^{-1}|E|\subseteq B$, every point of $|E|$ belongs to $\pi(B)$; hence $\rho^{-1}|E|\subseteq B_M$.

Apply [lem-per-noetherian-log-pair-strict-resolution] to $(M,B_M)$. It gives a proper birational $e:R\to M$, with $R$ integral regular Noetherian, and a strict normal crossings boundary $A$ satisfying $e^{-1}B_M\subseteq|A|$. Consequently $r=\rho e:R\to X$ is proper birational and $r^{-1}|E|\subseteq |A|$. The properness of the composite follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; birationality follows by intersecting the dense opens on which the two morphisms are isomorphisms.

We check the exact original boundary, rather than only containment in $A$. Locally $E$ has one nonzero equation $a$; its pullback to the integral scheme $R$ remains nonzero because $r$ is dominant. At a point of $R$, the resolution statement gives parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ for the components of $A$. The support inclusion means that $a$ is a unit after inverting $t_1\cdots t_s$. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization], $a=u\prod t_i^{n_i}$ for a unit $u$ and $n_i\geq0$. Its reduced support is the union of exactly the branches with $n_i>0$. These local descriptions show that the global reduced inverse image is a union of components of $A$: a selected branch contains an open subset of its integral component, whose closure lies in the closed inverse image. By [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], deleting components preserves the defining regular-intersection and codimension conditions, and the reduced local equation is the product of the selected distinct parameters, an effective Cartier ideal. Thus $r^{-1}|E|$ is precisely the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. If $s=0$, $a$ is a unit and that boundary is empty. This proves the marked nodal quotient assertion required in Step 1.

source.place: IX 2.4, last paragraph, p. 134; VIII 4.2.2(i), p. 118

proof.text: The implication in [lem-per-uniformization-nodal-quotient-reduction], now with its marked-model hypothesis proved, applies to the given $S,Z,\ell$. It produces a finite covering family $q_b:T_b\to S$ in $\operatorname{alt}/S$, with $T_b$ regular Noetherian and the exact support $q_b^{-1}Z$ a strict normal crossings boundary. By [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], objects of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ are finite-type morphisms. These are all clauses of the item. In particular no finite-dimensional or excellence assumption has been imposed on the original quasi-excellent $S$.
